# Flow 1 · The main flow, one template at a time

Back to the guide: [README.md](README.md) · all cases: [TEST-CASES.md](TEST-CASES.md). Mark each case in the app with `/tests` (p / f / s).

Every template walks the same gates, in this order:

| Gate | What you see and choose |
|---|---|
| Scope review | "Approve this scope manifest?" → Approve scope / Edit manifest / Reject (API also: Attach OpenAPI spec). Edit manifest is all or nothing; after Approve the scope is locked. Reject (red) has no number: a digit never picks it, use ↑/↓ and Enter. |
| Plan | "Run this plan?" → Run plan / Edit steps / Cancel (red, no number). The other rows run on their own; the target login (when the tools need one), 3a (MEDIUM) and 3b (HIGH) wait for you. |
| Target login | Only when the scope's tools need one (Web URL: account + one-time code; API: session cookie). What you type is never shown or saved. |
| MEDIUM approval | "Run <action> on <target>?" → Approve & run / Reject / View details / Edit params. Reject (red) has no number: use ↑/↓ and Enter. A rejected action is skipped and the plan goes on. On a short terminal the screen opens on the request; a note says to press ↓ for the choices. |
| HIGH approval | The same menu, then "◆ HIGH-RISK · second confirmation"; its default is No, go back. |
| Execution | One request outside the scope is proposed and blocked: "Blocked: … Not executed." Ctrl+C asks "Stop this assessment?". |
| Findings and report | 3 findings per template (Enter open, f filter, s sort, t triage); on the Report screen p PDF, j JSON, w DOCX once the run is complete (saved in apps/tui/reports/). |

**Test values:** any password (it never shows) and the one-time code `123456`. Type `/new` before each case.

## 1.1 Web URL (a website)

A URL like https://shop.example.com picks Web URL at once. A bare hostname asks "Which kind of target is it?".

| What this template sets up | |
|---|---|
| Scope | methods GET and POST; never touches /admin; tools Nuclei and OWASP ZAP; time limit 30 min |
| Login | email/username + password, then a 6-digit one-time code (OWASP ZAP needs it) |
| MEDIUM | Baseline request (read-only) · GET /api/orders/10482 |
| HIGH | Cross-account read check · GET /api/orders/10483 (test account B) |
| Blocked in the run | Blocked: GET /admin · Path outside approved scope. Not executed. |
| Findings | 001 MEDIUM Broken object-level authorization · 002 MEDIUM Reflected input in search page · 003 LOW Session cookie missing SameSite |

#### MF-WEB-01 · The whole flow, approve everything

**Type this:**

```text
Check https://shop.example.com for web security issues
```

1. Scope: "Approve this scope manifest?" → Approve scope → the scope is locked.
2. Plan: "Run this plan?" → Run plan.
3. Login: the login form opens. Email or username demo.tester, any password (it never shows) → Save login; then the one-time code 123456 → Submit code.
4. MEDIUM: "Run Baseline request (read-only) on …?" → Approve & run.
5. HIGH → Approve & run → "◆ HIGH-RISK · second confirmation" → move down to Yes, run … → Enter.
6. Execution: the log shows "Blocked: GET /admin · Path outside approved scope. Not executed."
7. Findings (Alt+6): 3 findings. Open 001 (Enter): evidence shows usr_••••42 and token: •••• (masked).
8. Report screen (Alt+8) → press p (PDF) → "✓ REPORT SAVED" shows the file path.

**Expected:** Every step on the step line ends at ✓; no password, token or cookie shows anywhere.

Result: ☐ Pass ☐ Fail ☐ Skip

#### MF-WEB-02 · Bare hostname: you pick the template

**Type this:**

```text
Assess staging.example.com
```

1. Template: "Which kind of target is it?" (4 choices) → Web URL.
2. Scope → Edit manifest → Excluded paths: /admin, /checkout · Time limit (minutes): 20 → Save scope.
3. The scope card now shows /checkout and 20 min → Approve scope → Run plan.
4. Login: the login form opens. Email or username demo.tester, any password (it never shows) → Save login; then the one-time code 123456 → Submit code.
5. MEDIUM → View details: scope limits, the exact request and its sha256 hash → Back to the choices → Approve & run.
6. HIGH → Approve & run → second confirmation → press Enter on the default No, go back → you are back at the approval; nothing ran.
7. HIGH → Approve & run → "◆ HIGH-RISK · second confirmation" → move down to Yes, run … → Enter.
8. Report screen (Alt+8) → press j (JSON) → "✓ REPORT SAVED" shows the file path.

**Expected:** The approved scope has /checkout and 20 min; the first "No, go back" ran nothing.

Result: ☐ Pass ☐ Fail ☐ Skip

#### MF-WEB-03 · Wrong scope values are refused

**Type this:**

```text
Scan the website https://shop.example.com
```

#### MF-WEB-04 · Edit the approval's parameters

**Type this:**

```text
Test https://shop.example.com for access control problems
```

1. Approve scope → Run plan → login (as MF-WEB-01).
2. MEDIUM → Edit params → /admin → Save params → "Blocked by policy: Path outside approved scope."
3. Edit params → /api/orders 10482 → "That path can't be used: one value, no spaces, at most 200 characters."
4. Edit params → /api/orders/10490 → accepted; the request now shows /api/orders/10490 → Approve & run.
5. HIGH → Approve & run → "◆ HIGH-RISK · second confirmation" → move down to Yes, run … → Enter.
6. Findings → open 002 → t (triage) → False positive → the list shows the new status.
7. Report screen (Alt+8) → press w (DOCX) → "✓ REPORT SAVED" shows the file path.

**Expected:** Blocked values never run; the accepted edit is what ran; the triage is in the report.

#### MF-WEB-05 · Reject at HIGH, the plan goes on

**Type this:**

```text
Check https://shop.example.com for web security issues
```

1. Approve scope → Run plan → login → MEDIUM Approve & run.
2. HIGH → Reject (↑/↓ then Enter; it has no number) → "Rejected: Cross-account read check. Not executed — the plan goes on with its next step." (on Execution's live output; scroll it up on a short terminal)
3. The run goes on to the end: "Assessment completed. 3 findings: 0 confirmed, 3 marked for review." and "Open the report (Alt+8 or /report) to export it."
4. /findings → 001 stays Unconfirmed: the validation that would confirm it was rejected.
5. Report screen (Alt+8) → press p (PDF) → "✓ REPORT SAVED" shows the file path.

**Expected:** Cross-account read check never runs; the same assessment completes and its report can be exported.

Result: ☐ Pass ☐ Fail ☐ Skip

## 1.2 API (REST / GraphQL)

A URL with an API path (/v1, /api, /graphql) or the word api, endpoints, swagger or openapi picks API at once.
The "API TEMPLATE: BASE URL AND SPEC" form opens first: press Esc to skip it (MF-API-02 attaches a spec).

| What this template sets up | |
|---|---|
| Scope | methods GET and POST; never touches /internal and /admin; tools Nuclei, Postman and ZAP API scan; time limit 30 min |
| Login | a session cookie (the API tools send it) |
| MEDIUM | Baseline request (read-only) · GET /v1/orders/8842 (token A) |
| HIGH | Cross-account read check · GET /v1/orders/8843 (token B's order) |
| Blocked in the run | Blocked: GET /internal/metrics · Path outside approved scope. Not executed. |
| Findings | 001 MEDIUM Broken object-level authorization · 002 MEDIUM Missing authorization on export endpoint · 003 LOW No rate limiting on login |

#### MF-API-01 · The whole flow, approve everything

**Type this:**

```text
Test the REST API at https://api.example.com/v1 for authorization issues
```

1. The "API TEMPLATE: BASE URL AND SPEC" form opens first: press Esc to skip it (MF-API-02 attaches a spec).
2. Scope → Approve scope → Plan → Run plan.
3. Login: Session cookie → type session=test-cookie-123 → Save login.
4. MEDIUM → Approve & run.
5. HIGH → Approve & run → "◆ HIGH-RISK · second confirmation" → move down to Yes, run … → Enter.
6. Execution: "Blocked: GET /internal/metrics · Path outside approved scope. Not executed."
7. Findings: 3 → Report screen (Alt+8) → press p (PDF) → "✓ REPORT SAVED" shows the file path.

**Expected:** Every step at ✓; the cookie value never shows in the log, the findings or the report.

Result: ☐ Pass ☐ Fail ☐ Skip

#### MF-API-02 · Attach an OpenAPI spec

**Type this:**

```text
Assess the api at api.example.com
```

1. The API form opens: keep the base URL, OpenAPI spec: scripts/sample/openapi-demo.yaml (reconix was started in apps/tui) → Save.
2. The scope review now offers Replace OpenAPI spec and Remove OpenAPI spec.
3. Remove OpenAPI spec → gone; Attach OpenAPI spec → the same file again.
4. A wrong path (nope.yaml) → "No file at that path."
5. Approve scope → Run plan → cookie → approve MEDIUM and HIGH.
6. Report screen (Alt+8) → press j (JSON) → "✓ REPORT SAVED" shows the file path.

**Expected:** The spec (4 endpoints, GET and POST) is read but never widens the scope.

Result: ☐ Pass ☐ Fail ☐ Skip

#### MF-API-03 · Reject the scope

**Type this:**

```text
Check https://api.example.com/v1 endpoints
```

1. The "API TEMPLATE: BASE URL AND SPEC" form opens first: press Esc to skip it (MF-API-02 attaches a spec).
2. Scope → Reject (↑/↓ then Enter; it has no number) → the toast "Scope rejected — nothing was tested."
3. You stay in the same assessment: the Template step shows ✕, the screen says "◆ reconix this assessment stopped before testing: you rejected the scope" and asks "Start again?" (Start a new assessment / Back to the start).
4. Ctrl+O on Execution (or /audit) → "Scope rejected. Nothing was tested." and "Assessment stopped. Nothing else will run. Type /new to start a new assessment."
5. /audit → the rejection is in the audit trail.
6. "Start again?" → Start a new assessment → /assessments still lists the rejected one as Stopped.

**Expected:** Nothing ran: no plan step started and there are no findings. Reject never opens a new assessment by itself.

Result: ☐ Pass ☐ Fail ☐ Skip

#### MF-API-04 · Edit the scope, find the blocked request in the audit

**Type this:**

```text
Test https://api.example.com/v1 for API security issues
```

1. The "API TEMPLATE: BASE URL AND SPEC" form opens first: press Esc to skip it (MF-API-02 attaches a spec).
2. Scope → Edit manifest → Allowed methods: GET, POST, DELETE · Excluded paths: /internal, /admin, /v1/admin → Save.
3. Edit manifest → Excluded paths: v1/x → "Excluded paths start with '/': v1/x."
4. Approve scope → Run plan → cookie → approve MEDIUM and HIGH.
5. /audit → the blocked GET /internal/metrics is listed with its reason.
6. Report → p (PDF): the exported report's scope section lists DELETE and /v1/admin.

**Expected:** The exported report shows exactly the scope you approved; the blocked request is in the audit trail.

Result: ☐ Pass ☐ Fail ☐ Skip

#### MF-API-05 · Reject at MEDIUM

**Type this:**

```text
Test the REST API at https://api.example.com/v1 for authorization issues
```

1. The "API TEMPLATE: BASE URL AND SPEC" form opens first: press Esc to skip it (MF-API-02 attaches a spec).
2. Approve scope → Run plan → cookie.
3. MEDIUM → Reject (↑/↓ then Enter) → the app goes straight to the HIGH approval, which shows "✕ Skipped: Baseline request (read-only) (rejected)". The line "Rejected: Baseline request (read-only). Not executed — the plan goes on with its next step." is in the Execution log (Ctrl+O) and in /audit.
4. The HIGH step still asks for its own approval: Approve & run → second confirmation → Yes.
5. The run completes: "Assessment completed. …" /audit lists approval.rejected for the MEDIUM step.

**Expected:** The rejected MEDIUM request never runs; the plan goes on and HIGH runs only after its own approval.

Result: ☐ Pass ☐ Fail ☐ Skip

## 1.3 Network (IP address or range)

An IPv4 address or CIDR range (10.0.0.0/24, 192.0.2.10) picks Network at once. Ports typed in the question fill the scope.

| What this template sets up | |
|---|---|
| Scope | TCP connect; ports 22, 80, 443, 8080 and 8443; tools nmap and testssl.sh; time limit 30 min; no login |
| MEDIUM | Banner and TLS check (read-only) · TCP 10.0.0.1:8443 |
| HIGH | Default login probe · one default credential on /manager |
| Blocked in the run | Blocked: TCP 198.51.100.9 · Host outside approved scope. Not executed. |
| Findings | 001 HIGH Management console exposed · 002 MEDIUM Deprecated TLS 1.0 offered · 003 LOW SSH banner reveals version |

#### MF-NET-01 · The whole flow, approve everything

**Type this:**

```text
Scan 10.0.0.0/24 for open ports and weak services
```

1. Scope → Approve scope → Plan → Run plan (no login step).
2. MEDIUM → Approve & run.
3. HIGH → Approve & run → "◆ HIGH-RISK · second confirmation" → move down to Yes, run … → Enter.
4. Execution: "Blocked: TCP 198.51.100.9 · Host outside approved scope. Not executed."
5. Findings: 001 HIGH, 002 MEDIUM, 003 LOW → Report screen (Alt+8) → press p (PDF) → "✓ REPORT SAVED" shows the file path.

**Expected:** Every step at ✓ and no login was asked.

Result: ☐ Pass ☐ Fail ☐ Skip

#### MF-NET-02 · Ports in the question fill the scope

**Type this:**

```text
scan 192.0.2.0/28 ports 22, 443 and 8443 with nmap
```

1. Scope card: Ports 22, 443 and 8443 (only the ones you typed).
2. Approve scope → Run plan → approve MEDIUM and HIGH.
3. Findings and the report use only those ports.

**Expected:** The scope, findings and report hold exactly ports 22, 443 and 8443.

Result: ☐ Pass ☐ Fail ☐ Skip

#### MF-NET-03 · Wrong addresses are refused

**Type this:**

```text
scan 10.0.0.300
```

1. scan 10.0.0.300 → "10.0.0.300 isn't a valid IPv4 address — four numbers from 0 to 255."
2. scan 10.0.0.0/8 → "10.0.0.0/8 is too wide to test — use a /16 or smaller range."
3. scan 10.0.0.20-10.0.0.1 → "… runs backwards — put the lower address first …"
4. scan 10.0.0.1-10.0.0.20 → "Dash ranges aren't supported by the scope yet — use CIDR, e.g. 10.0.0.0/27."
5. scan my network → "Network needs an IPv4 address or range, or a hostname — e.g. 10.0.0.0/24"
6. Each refused line stays in the prompt, selected: typing replaces it (type /new and the command list opens instead of adding to the address).
7. Then scan 10.0.0.0/28 → accepted → finish the flow.

**Expected:** Each bad address shows its message and nothing starts; the CIDR range starts.

Result: ☐ Pass ☐ Fail ☐ Skip

#### MF-NET-04 · Scope edit and ports suggested in chat

**Type this:**

```text
Scan 10.0.0.0/24 for open ports
```

1. Scope → Edit manifest → Allowed ports 0 → "Not a valid port (1–65535): 0."; 99999 → the same; empty → "Keep at least one allowed port."
2. Excluded 10.0.0.0/33 → "Exclude a host, range or host:port (e.g. 10.0.0.5:22): 10.0.0.0/33."; Excluded 10.0.0.5:22 → Save scope.
3. Chat about this → type add port 3389 → "Only you can change the scope. Tick what it allows, then press Enter to save." and a tick list with 3389 unticked; the list opens on the 3389 row.
4. Press Space (ticks 3389), then Enter → the scope card shows port 3389.
5. Type add ports 1-1024 → "The scope lists single ports, not a range (1-1024)…"; add 10.0.0.99 to the scope → "Hosts can't change here…" (no tick list).
6. Approve scope → Run plan → finish.

**Expected:** Only your tick changed the scope; the wrong values changed nothing.

Result: ☐ Pass ☐ Fail ☐ Skip

#### MF-NET-05 · The HIGH double check and blocked parameters

**Type this:**

```text
Check 10.0.0.0/24 for exposed management consoles
```

1. Approve scope → Run plan → MEDIUM Approve & run.
2. HIGH → Edit params → 10.9.9.9:22 → "Blocked by policy: Host outside approved scope."
3. 10.0.0.7:8081 → "Blocked by policy: Port 8081 not in the approved list."
4. 10.0.0.7 → "Give a host and a port, e.g. 10.0.0.1:8443."
5. 10.0.0.7:8443 → accepted.
6. Approve & run → second confirmation → No, go back (nothing runs) → Approve & run → Yes.
7. Findings → f → Critical & High → open 001 (on 10.0.0.1:8443): it stays UNCONFIRMED with the evidence "Not collected: the check ran on 10.0.0.7:8443, not on this finding's own host and port, so it can't confirm it." → Report screen (Alt+8) → press w (DOCX) → "✓ REPORT SAVED" shows the file path.

**Expected:** Only an in-scope host:port can be set; HIGH runs only after the second Yes; a check moved to another host never confirms the finding.

Result: ☐ Pass ☐ Fail ☐ Skip

## 1.4 Source Code (git repo or folder)

A git repo (https://…/x.git, git@host:owner/repo, github.com/owner/repo) or a local folder path picks Source Code at once.

| What this template sets up | |
|---|---|
| Scope | read only; never touches .git, node_modules, vendor and secrets; tools Semgrep, gitleaks and pip-audit; no login |
| MEDIUM | Read the flagged line (read-only) · app/config/settings.py:42 |
| HIGH | Check the flagged credential once · one try on a test database |
| Blocked in the run | Blocked: read .git/config · Path excluded from the review. Not executed. |
| Findings | 001 HIGH Hardcoded database password · 002 MEDIUM SQL built by string concatenation · 003 LOW Vulnerable dependency |

#### MF-SRC-01 · The whole flow, approve everything

**Type this:**

```text
Review the repo https://git.example.com/acme/app.git for secrets and insecure code
```

1. Scope → Approve scope → Plan → Run plan.
2. MEDIUM → Approve & run.
3. HIGH → Approve & run → "◆ HIGH-RISK · second confirmation" → move down to Yes, run … → Enter.
4. Execution: "Blocked: read .git/config · Path excluded from the review. Not executed."
5. Findings → open 001: the password is masked (••••) → Report screen (Alt+8) → press p (PDF) → "✓ REPORT SAVED" shows the file path.

**Expected:** Every step at ✓; the hardcoded password never shows in plain text.

Result: ☐ Pass ☐ Fail ☐ Skip

#### MF-SRC-02 · Other ways to name a repository

**Type this:**

```text
review git@git.example.com:acme/app.git
```

1. review git@git.example.com:acme/app.git → Source Code.
2. /new → scan the source code in ./demo-app → Source Code (a folder path).
3. /new → review repo github.com/acme → "github.com/acme isn't a repository — e.g. github.com/acme/app".
4. /new → the first line again → finish the flow.

**Expected:** All repository forms are understood; the incomplete one is explained.

Result: ☐ Pass ☐ Fail ☐ Skip

#### MF-SRC-03 · Paths that leave the repository are blocked

**Type this:**

```text
Check https://git.example.com/acme/app.git for hardcoded secrets
```

1. Approve scope → Run plan.
2. MEDIUM → Edit params → ../../etc/passwd → "Blocked by policy: Path leaves the repository."
3. /etc/passwd and ~/.ssh/id_rsa → "Give a file in the repository, e.g. app/config/settings.py."
4. secrets/prod.env → "Blocked by policy: Path excluded from the review."
5. app/db/queries.py → accepted → Approve & run.
6. HIGH → Approve & run → "◆ HIGH-RISK · second confirmation" → move down to Yes, run … → Enter.

**Expected:** Only files inside the repository and outside the excluded paths can be read.

Result: ☐ Pass ☐ Fail ☐ Skip

#### MF-SRC-04 · Reorder the gated checks in the plan

**Type this:**

```text
Review https://git.example.com/acme/app.git for security issues
```

1. Approve scope → at the plan: Chat about this → move 3b before 3a → "Only you can change the order…" and an order list.
2. Move "Check the flagged credential once" up (Shift+↑) → Enter → "Plan updated" and the plan card shows 3a Check the flagged credential once (HIGH), 3b Read the flagged line (MEDIUM).
3. Type move step 1 to the end → the order list again: only the gated checks can move; phases 1–5 stay fixed.
4. Run plan → HIGH is asked first, then MEDIUM → approve both.
5. Report screen (Alt+8) → press j (JSON) → "✓ REPORT SAVED" shows the file path.

**Expected:** The run follows the order you saved; the phases never move.

Result: ☐ Pass ☐ Fail ☐ Skip

#### MF-SRC-05 · Stop during the run

**Type this:**

```text
Review the repo https://git.example.com/acme/app.git for secrets and insecure code
```

1. Approve scope → Run plan → while it runs press Ctrl+C → "Stop this assessment?" → Keep running → it goes on.
2. Ctrl+C again → Stop now → "You stopped it. Nothing else will run."
3. /findings → only what was found so far. /summary → the stop.
4. /new → start again.

**Expected:** Keep running loses nothing; Stop now runs nothing else and keeps what was found.

Result: ☐ Pass ☐ Fail ☐ Skip
